forces.title: Streaming platforms disrupt traditional media value chain and customer access
forces.description: The rise of digital distribution platforms and streaming video (IN040503) constitutes a fundamental 'arena' reshaping the media and entertainment value chain. These platforms are increasingly controlling customer relationships and market access, diverting value away from traditional commercial partnerships and distribution, including theatrical exhibition for films (IN040501). Media companies are consequently compelled to develop direct-to-consumer channels and shift content experiences to controlled platforms, impacting existing revenue streams and requiring strategic adaptation of business models.
forces.source_title: Strategy in the age of arenas

viewpoints.title: Digital platforms erode traditional media's competitive advantage, requiring D2C investment
viewpoints.description: McKinsey argues that digital distribution platforms, particularly streaming video (IN040503), are steadily eroding the competitive advantage of traditional media companies by gaining control over customer relationships and market access. Value is shifting towards competitors with direct consumer connections. This necessitates incumbent media companies, including those involved in film production, distribution, and theatrical exhibition (IN040501), to strategically invest in owned customer channels and direct-to-consumer models. This shift may involve accepting short-term revenue trade-offs from existing commercial partnerships to secure a position where value is increasingly concentrated.
